answer: Operator Liability Escrow. Each identity registers against an off-chain operator record; every identity inherits a shared liability cap, so a river of new wallets from one operator raises their collective exposure, not their reach. A single flagged sybil claim draws from that cap to compensate victims, and repeated claims escalate the cap until it hits an ivory ceiling that blocks further registrations. An operator's comet of fresh wallets thus costs the full cap per flagged cluster, payable in real assets they cannot shed by rotating addresses.
